status: Installed; controlled receive checks pass. Actual writable Armbian boot initially entered emergency mode with media connected; the offered Ctrl-D continuation subsequently reached automatic root login and interactive first-boot password setup without a reboot or reconnect.

scope.faultProbes: Trusted TLS/WSS with HELLO, synthetic ECHO and HEARTBEAT only; no INSERT, HID or image reads
scope.actualBootMeasurement: Passive HTTP80 diagnostics during a pre-fix failed browser-backed Armbian boot and a post-fix writable boot attempt; only the latter has a known target-restart marker
notEstablished: Unattended normal startup without emergency-mode intervention
Post-account-setup OS health and the initial failed startup dependency
Completed-boot duration or causal whole-boot throughput improvement

fix.scope: Remaining WebSocket header plus payload after IDF has consumed the initial opcode byte, scoped to the same HTTP task, request and socket
fix.initialOpcodeByte: Retains the original server receive timeout before the application handler
fix.deadline: One absolute monotonic deadline shared across header, mask, payload and every underlying TLS BIO receive; progress and retries do not renew it
fix.socketTimeoutRestoration: Restored immediately after each underlying HTTP receive and retried at scope end on failure
fix.retryCpuPolicy: Yield one scheduler tick without extending the deadline
fix.pendingPrefixHandling: Return HTTPD pending bytes separately before a subsequent TLS read can return a raw WANT code
fix.httpAndExplicitPendingOnlyPassThrough: Unchanged outside a matched active receive; same task/fd plus receiving flag scopes BIO hook
unchangedGuards: USB epoch and stale request checks

payloadGap.interpretation: The former roughly two-second payload receive cutoff is reproduced by the controlled gap; the installed fix accepts that same delayed payload with validated CRC, offset and bytes and successful heartbeat.
payloadGap.beforeFirmwareStage: Previous installed 32 KiB build, before scoped frame receive fix

absoluteDeadline.interpretation: Expected failure: peer closes near the ten-second total receive budget instead of waiting for the eleven-second remainder.

splitHeaderRegression.scope: Legacy unsplit, 20 ms split-mask and split-extended-length checks on the installed frame fix; log does not record payload size

cases: Delayed 32 KiB payload and short header reads share one deadline
Pending prefix followed by raw TLS WANT preserves every byte
A single TLS read with eight one-second BIO fragments succeeds at eight seconds
A single TLS read with progressing 1.5-second BIO fragments stops at ten seconds
Same-task/exact-fd active receive scope; other task/fd and explicit pending-only calls preserve socket settings
Positive data arriving at or after the deadline is rejected
Socket timeout setup/restoration failure, EOF and fatal errors fail closed
First failure preserved and frame-timeout counter increments once

measurementThroughFirstEmergencyObservat.status: Normal startup did not complete; emergency mode and later service timeouts were observed while the virtual-media session stayed active
limitations: This is a measured failed normal boot attempt, not a complete boot duration or a completed-OS throughput result
The endpoint is the last diagnostic before the emergency-mode observation; the adjacent sample brackets counters at that visual observation
Service timeouts may stem from image/service settings or be aggravated by slow virtual-disk IO; stable transport does not identify their cause
Cumulative remote bytes include read-ahead and repeated reads and are not unique USB bytes; cache hits are separate

targetEventOrdering.interpretation: The emergency-mode event precedes these two named service timeouts. The timeouts cannot be asserted to have caused the emergency transition without further journal evidence.
